[{"node": "menu_content106", "element": "menu_content", "data": {"label": "Kitchen", "key": "kitchen_menu_content", "id": "kitchen_menu_content", "name": "kitchen_menu_content"}, "elements": [{"node": "markdown101", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Production centers", "key": "md_production_centers", "id": "production-centers", "name": "md_production_centers", "value": "# Production centers

A **production center** (kitchen, grill, bar, coffee, expo…) prepares some item groups. Each one is configured in its own form:

- the **item groups** it prepares (child groups included);
- its **status flow**, in order (see below);
- **Group Items By Order**: handle a whole ticket with one tap instead of item by item;
- optional restrictions to some rooms, tables or branches;
- its **ticket printer** and color.

A floor can have as many centers as you need, and a person only sees the centers they were given (or all of them, for managers).
"}}, {"node": "markdown102", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Statuses and flows", "key": "md_statuses_and_flows", "id": "statuses-and-flows", "name": "md_statuses_and_flows", "value": "# Statuses and flows

Nothing in the flow is fixed. Each **status** (Status Order PC) defines:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Status** | Its internal name, e.g. *Sent*, *Attending*, *Ready* |
| **Shown As** | How screens show an item in that status, e.g. *Waiting* |
| **Action** | The verb that **leads to** this status, e.g. *Send*, *Take*, *Complete* |
| **Color** | Used on cards, chips and the floor-plan dock |
| **Waiter Can Edit** | Lines in this status can still be changed by the server |

A center's flow is a list of statuses, for example *Sent → Attending → Ready → Delivered*. Items arrive in the first one and leave the screen in the last one. A card always shows the **current status** and a button with the **action of the next status**: an item *Waiting* shows **Take**; once taken it shows **Complete**.

Statuses the server can still edit can't be part of a production flow, so the kitchen never sees items that weren't sent.
"}}, {"node": "markdown103", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Chaining centers", "key": "md_chaining_centers", "id": "chaining-centers", "name": "md_chaining_centers", "value": "# Chaining centers

The status lives on the **order line** and is shared by every center that handles it. Centers can be chained by status: the coffee bar moves a latte *Sent → Ready*, and the expo / dining-room center (*Ready → Delivered*) picks it up. Every screen showing that line refreshes in real time, including the server's order.
"}}, {"node": "markdown104", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "The center screen", "key": "md_the_center_screen", "id": "the-center-screen", "name": "md_the_center_screen", "value": "# The center screen

Tap a center in the **Production** column (or bar, on phones). Tickets show the table, room, server, guests, round number, notes, and each item with its options and notes, oldest first.

- Tap an item (or the ticket, for grouped centers) to move it to the next status.
- If another screen moved it first, Ren tells you instead of moving it twice.
- **Recall** shows what was just completed and lets you **undo** it.
- Voided items appear crossed out for a few minutes so the cook stops preparing them.
- A sound announces new tickets.
"}}, {"node": "markdown105", "element": "markdown", "data": {"label": "Printed tickets", "key": "md_printed_tickets", "id": "printed-tickets", "name": "md_printed_tickets", "value": "# Printed tickets

When an order is sent, each center with a printer gets a ticket with only its items: quantity, options, notes, the order note and the server. Voids print a void ticket. If a printer is off, the order is still sent and the person who sent it is offered a retry.
"}}]}]
